texts.li: A small jar of something dark and pickled stopped {A_nameDef} dead in front of the peddler's blanket. It's a food from where {A_nameDef} grew up, and {A_pronoun} hasn't seen it, or smelled it, in years.\n\n{X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, who spread the blanket out by the gate this morning, wants {COUNT} silver for the jar and the rest of the crate it came from.

[past:farmer] {A_nameDef} knew the grain by its smell before the sack was even open. It's the same kind {A_possessive} family grew, from the same valley, and {A_nameDef} has had a handful of it in {A_possessive} pocket all morning.\n\n{X_nameDef}, a peddler of {FACTION}, wants {COUNT} silver for the sack and the jars of preserves that came with it.

[past:soldier] At the bottom of a peddler's crate, {A_nameDef} found a tin of the hard biscuit {A_possessive} old regiment lived on for years. Anyone else would call it inedible. {A_nameDef} is holding it like a letter from home.\n\n{X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, the peddler, wants {COUNT} silver for the tin and the crate it came in.

[past:noble] "We drank this in the garden," {A_nameDef} says, turning the box of tea over in {A_possessive} hands, "every afternoon, under the pear tree." It's the first word {A_nameDef} has said about that house since coming here.\n\n{X_nameDef}, a peddler of {FACTION}, wants {COUNT} silver for the tea and the rest of the box.

[past:trader] {A_nameDef} used to trade in this spice, a long way from here, and caught the smell of it from across the yard. {X_nameDef}, a peddler of {FACTION}, has a whole sack of it, and wants {COUNT} silver.\n\n{A_nameDef}, who haggles over everything, hasn't haggled over this.

[lowtech] Honey cakes, made the way they make them in {A_nameDef}'s home valley, with seeds on top and a burnt edge. {X_nameDef}, a peddler of {FACTION}, has a basket of them. {A_nameDef} bought one on the spot, ate it in three bites, and wants the basket, for {COUNT} silver.

[spacer] The label on the tins is one {A_nameDef} hasn't seen since leaving {A_possessive} home system. {X_nameDef}, a peddler of {FACTION}, has a whole crate of them. It probably isn't good fish. {A_nameDef} wants it anyway, all of it, for {COUNT} silver.

[industrial] The rest of the colony won't go near the sweet brown paste in {X_nameDef}'s crate. {A_nameDef} grew up on it, and has already had a finger in the first jar. {X_nameDef}, a peddler of {FACTION}, wants {COUNT} silver for the crate.

li.label: Buy it for {A_nameDef} ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} ate the first of it standing up at the gate, and has been rationing the rest ever since.

outcomes.li: [trait:Kind] {A_nameDef} took the crate round the colony and made each of them try some, explaining every time exactly what it was and where it came from.
[trait:Greedy] {A_nameDef} carried the crate straight to {A_possessive} room and has not been seen sharing any of it.
[past:soldier] {A_nameDef} ate one of the biscuits with water, the old way, and didn't say anything for a long while afterwards.

li.label: Buy it, and let {A_nameDef} cook it for everyone ({COUNT} silver, 10 food)
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} took over the kitchen for an evening and made the colony a supper from home, standing at the end of the table to explain each dish as it came out. The colony asked for the sour one again.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] {A_nameDef} cooked the way {A_possessive} grandmother did, on hot stones, and told the story of every dish while it was eaten.
[trait:Gourmand] {A_nameDef} cooked for most of the day and tasted everything twice. The colony ate well, and {A_nameDef} ate better.

li.label: {A_nameDef} can live without it
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} lingers by the blanket a while, then goes back to work.

outcomes.li: [colony:Thrifty] The colony doesn't spend silver on luxuries. {A_nameDef} knows that, and walks away from the blanket without arguing.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} went very still when the name was said. {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} is at the gate, asking for {A_objective}. They knew each other once, before the colony, and it didn't end well.\n\n{X_nameDef} wants to apologize, and to put something right, if {A_nameDef} will allow it.

[past:soldier] In the war {A_nameDef} doesn't talk about, {X_nameDef} fought on the other side. They met once, across a field, and both of them remember it.\n\n{X_nameDef} is with {FACTION} now, and has walked for weeks to say what {X_pronoun} couldn't say then. {X_nameDef} asks for an hour of {A_nameDef}'s time.

[past:outlaw] Years ago, {X_nameDef} sold {A_nameDef} out to the law for a reward and a pardon, and {A_nameDef} did time for it. Now {X_nameDef}, who is with {FACTION} these days, is at the gate with a bundle under one arm, asking very quietly to talk.

[past:noble] The rumor {X_nameDef} spread at court wasn't true, everyone involved knew it, and it ruined {A_nameDef}'s family all the same. {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} is old now, and has come all this way to ask {A_nameDef}'s forgiveness in person.

[past:trader] "I owe you a cargo," {X_nameDef} says at the gate, "and eleven years." {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} cheated {A_nameDef} out of that cargo once, and left {A_objective} in debt for most of those years. Now {X_nameDef} has a purse and an apology, and is asking for {A_nameDef}.

[past:healer] A patient died, years ago, and {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} blamed {A_nameDef} for it, loudly, with everyone who mattered listening. It wasn't {A_nameDef}'s fault. {X_nameDef} has come to say so, years late.

[past:scholar] The work that made {X_nameDef}'s name was {A_nameDef}'s. {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} put {X_possessive} own name on it and built a career on top. Now {X_nameDef} has come to the colony to admit it, and to ask what can be done.

[past:artisan] {A_nameDef} lost a workshop because of {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, who copied {A_possessive} designs years ago and sold them for twice the price. {X_nameDef} is at the gate now, hat in hand, asking to talk.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} hear {X_objective} out
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {X_nameDef} talked behind a closed door for most of the afternoon. When they came out, {X_nameDef} left a bundle on the table and went. {A_nameDef} was humming at supper.

outcomes.li: [past:soldier] They talked about the field, and the day, and who they'd each lost there. {X_nameDef} left something on the table before going. That night {A_nameDef} slept straight through.
[past:trader] {X_nameDef} counted out what the old cargo was worth, with interest, on the table between them. {A_nameDef} counted it again, then shook {X_nameDef}'s hand.
[trait:Kind] {A_nameDef} forgave {X_nameDef} before {X_nameDef} had finished the apology, and then made {X_objective} finish it anyway.

li.riskOutcome: It didn't go well. The old wound went deeper than either of them thought, and {A_nameDef} came out of the room before the hour was up and asked {X_nameDef} to leave. {X_nameDef} did.

li.label: Ask {X_objective} to stay for supper
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} stayed for supper, and the rest of the colony made enough noise around the two of them that it was easier to talk. By the end of the evening {A_nameDef} and {X_nameDef} were trading stories about people they both knew.

li.label: {A_nameDef} wants nothing from {X_objective}
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} waits at the gate until dusk, then leaves.

outcomes.li: [trait:Abrasive] {A_nameDef} told {X_nameDef} exactly what {A_pronoun} thought of the apology, at length, and {X_nameDef} left before supper.
[trait:Kind] {A_nameDef} wouldn't see {X_nameDef}, but sent a loaf of bread out to the gate before dark.

texts.li: On the way in, {X_nameDef} stopped at the colony's graves and stood there a while with {X_possessive} hat in {X_possessive} hands. {X_nameDef} cuts stone for {FACTION}, and says the colony's dead are marked with sticks and rough stones. For {COUNT} silver, each could have a proper headstone, with the name cut deep enough to last.

[tribal] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} raises cairns over the dead, the way the old tribes do, carrying the stones a long way so the spirits know they were loved. {X_nameDef} has walked past the colony's graves twice now, slowly, and offers to raise a proper cairn over each one, for {COUNT} silver or its worth in goods.

[medieval] {X_nameDef}, a stonemason of {FACTION}, carries a mallet worn smooth by years of lettering. The colony's graves are marked with whatever came to hand, {X_nameDef} says, and the dead deserve better. For {COUNT} silver, there will be a proper stone for each, with the name on it.

[industrial] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} engraves headstones, and travels with a box of chisels and a roll of rubbings taken from other people's graveyards. {X_nameDef} looked at the colony's graves with professional disapproval, and offers to mark every one properly for {COUNT} silver.

[spacer] {X_nameDef}, a memorial-maker of {FACTION}, carries a laser etcher and a stack of polished stone blanks. For {COUNT} silver, every grave in the colony will have a proper marker by tomorrow: a name, two dates and a line about each, if someone will say what it should be.

{X_nameDef} of {FACTION} cuts stone for the dead, and has already been round the colony's graves once with a stick of chalk, marking the head of each. The price is {COUNT} silver for a proper marker on every one.

A traveler of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef}, asked who was buried in the colony's graveyard, and listened to every name. For {COUNT} silver, {X_nameDef} offers to cut each of those names in stone, so the next people to come this way will know them too.

li.label: A proper marker for every grave ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} worked through the evening and into the next morning, and {A_nameDef} sat by the graves telling the stonecutter about each of the dead, so the stones would say the right thing.

outcomes.li: [tribal] {X_nameDef} raised a cairn over every grave, and the colony carried stones to {X_objective} all afternoon. By dark the graveyard looked like a place someone had cared for.
[spacer] The etcher hummed all evening. By morning every grave had a polished stone with a name, two dates, and a line {A_nameDef} chose for each.
[colony:Traditional] The colony gathered at the graves when the last stone was set, and {A_nameDef} read the names out, one by one.

li.label: Have {X_objective} teach our best crafter how (half that)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} showed {B_nameDef} how to split a stone along its grain and cut a letter that won't weather away. {B_nameDef} has been practicing on offcuts since, and means to mark the graves personally.

outcomes.li: [b:skill:Artistic] {B_nameDef} took to the chisel as if born holding one. {X_nameDef} said so, twice, which {B_nameDef} will be repeating for weeks.

li.label: Our dead are well enough as they are
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} nods, says a few words over the graves anyway, and goes on in the morning.

texts.li: High water took out the bridge below {PLACE}. {FACTION} have the timber cut and waiting, but none of them knows how to make a span that won't go into the river again.\n\nA rider brought their request this morning: the colony's best builder, for a day of advice and drawings, for {COUNT} silver.

[lowtech] The rope bridge over the gorge near {PLACE} snapped in the last storm, and {FACTION} are cut off from their summer pastures. The runner their elders sent wants to know whether the colony has someone who can hang a bridge that will hold a laden mule. They'll pay {COUNT} silver for a day of that someone's advice.

[medieval] The mill wheel at {PLACE} has broken its axle, and {FACTION}'s miller says there'll be no flour until it's set right. Their carpenters have the timber but not the know-how. Could the colony lend them a builder for a day, to look at the drawings and tell them how? They'll pay {COUNT} silver.
[industrial] The note that came with {FACTION}'s drawings reads, in full: "Water tower at {PLACE} leaning. Crew won't climb it. Need a builder's eye, one day. Will pay {COUNT} silver."

[spacer] A storm buckled the mast of the wind turbine at {PLACE}, and {FACTION} have been running on batteries since. Their crew have the parts and not the experience. They'll pay {COUNT} silver for a day of advice from the colony's best builder.

[winter] The roof of the meeting hall at {PLACE} came down under the snow, and {FACTION} want it back up before the next fall of it. They've sent their plans and a request: a day of advice from the colony's best builder, for {COUNT} silver.

{FACTION}'s builders have been arguing for a week about how to rebuild the washed-out crossing near {PLACE}, and the crossing is still washed out. They'd like the colony's best builder to spend a day with them and settle it, and they'll pay {COUNT} silver.

A roll of drawings came up from {PLACE} this morning, with {FACTION}'s mark on the outside and a question inside. Something they built has failed, and they want someone who knows building to tell them why. For a day of advice, they offer {COUNT} silver.

li.label: Lend them our best builder
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} spent the day over {FACTION}'s drawings with their carpenters, redrew half of them and sent them home with a plan that will stand. The silver came back with their messenger.

outcomes.li: [b:trait:Abrasive] {B_nameDef} told {FACTION}'s carpenters exactly what was wrong with their plans, and they didn't enjoy it. The plan {B_nameDef} drew them will stand, though, and they paid.
[b:past:artisan] {B_nameDef} learned the trade in a proper workshop, and it showed. {FACTION}'s carpenters went home with a set of drawings they'll be copying for years.

li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef}'s plan was sound, but {FACTION}'s carpenters only followed half of it. What they built stands, more or less, and they paid half the silver and kept the rest for repairs.

li.label: Send them timber instead (80 wood)
li.outcome: The colony hauled the timber down to the gate for {FACTION} to collect and take to {PLACE}. They paid what they could for it, and will have to work out the rest themselves.

li.label: We can't spare anyone
li.outcome: Word goes back to {PLACE} that the colony can't spare anyone. {FACTION} will manage, or they won't.

texts.li: Half of {X_nameDef}'s herd is off its feed and coughing, and the rest won't be far behind. {X_nameDef}, a herder of {FACTION}, came at a run when someone on the road said the colony has a hand with animals.\n\n{X_nameDef} would pay {COUNT} silver for a look at them, or take whatever medicine the colony can spare.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} drives goats along the high pastures, and three days ago the goats started to sicken: dull eyes, runny noses, no appetite. {X_nameDef} has left the herd in the lee of a hill and come down to the colony alone, asking for anyone who knows animals. {COUNT} silver, {X_nameDef} says, for a look.

[!lowtech] {X_nameDef}, a herder of {FACTION}, came to the gate with a list of symptoms written on the back of a feed receipt. The herd's vet died last winter and the replacement never came. {X_nameDef} would pay {COUNT} silver for someone who knows animals to come and look.

[tundra] The reindeer are coughing. {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} herds them, and the nearest help is a week's walk away, {X_nameDef} says, while the colony is right here. {COUNT} silver for a look at them, or a little medicine.

[desert] {X_nameDef}, a camel driver of {FACTION}, has left the string hobbled down the road. Two of the camels have a fever and the rest are going the same way. {X_nameDef} would pay {COUNT} silver for someone who knows animals.

[spring] It's the birthing season, the worst time for a sickness to get into a herd, and one has got into {X_nameDef}'s. {X_nameDef}, a herder of {FACTION}, asks if the colony's best with animals could come and look, for {COUNT} silver.

li.label: Send our best with animals
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} went out to the herd with {X_nameDef} and spent the day dosing, listening to chests and cutting a few out to keep apart. Most of them were eating again by evening. {X_nameDef} paid gladly.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] {B_nameDef} boiled up a bitter mash of herbs and dosed the goats one by one, with {X_nameDef} holding the heads. By evening most of them were nosing at the grass again.
[b:past:farmer] {B_nameDef} grew up with a herd and knew the cough the moment {B_pronoun} heard it. A day's dosing, and the herd was on the mend.

li.riskOutcome: It was a bad fever, and slow to turn. {B_nameDef} saw the worst cases through, but the herd will be weak for weeks. {X_nameDef} paid what could be spared.

li.label: Sell {X_objective} medicine (2)
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} paid for two doses of the colony's medicine and hurried back to the herd with them.

li.label: Wish {X_objective} luck
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} goes back to the herd alone.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} walked over from the camp {PLACE} to say it's been a good week out there, and the camp means to mark it with whatever is in the pot. The colony is invited to the fire tonight.
[camp:Hunters] The hunters camped {PLACE} brought down something big this morning, and tonight they're roasting it whole. {X_nameDef} came over to say the colony is welcome at the fire.
[camp:Pilgrims] It's a holy day for the pilgrims camped {PLACE}, and on holy days they feed whoever comes. {X_nameDef} has invited the colony to eat with them tonight.

[camp:Market] "Best week we've had since the coast," {X_nameDef} says, and the traders' stall {PLACE} is closing early to mark it. There'll be food and drink at the camp tonight, and the colony is invited.
[camp:Refugees] The family camped {PLACE} has little enough, but it's {X_nameDef}'s birthday, and they mean to mark it. They've asked the colony to come and share what they have.
[camp:Smith] The smith camped {PLACE} finished a piece today that {X_nameDef} says is the best of the year, and the camp means to drink to it tonight. The colony is invited.
[camp:Prospectors] The prospectors camped {PLACE} found color in the pan this morning, real color, and they're celebrating as if they'd struck it rich. {X_nameDef} came over to invite the colony.
[camp:Hermit] The hermit {PLACE}, {X_nameDef}, has done something unheard of and invited the colony over. It's {X_nameDef}'s birthday, and it's been a long time since anyone noticed.

li.label: Go, and bring food (20 food)
li.outcome: The colony walked over at dusk with a sack of food, and the camp made room at the fire. It was a long, loud evening, and the walk home was a slow one.

outcomes.li: [camp:Hermit] The colony turned up with food and a song, and {X_nameDef} didn't know what to do with either. By the end of the night {X_nameDef} was singing too.
[winter] The colony brought food over through the snow, and the camp's fire was built so high that the guests sat in shirtsleeves.

li.label: Go, and enjoy their hospitality
li.outcome: The colony went over at dusk empty-handed and was fed anyway, from the camp's pot, at the camp's fire. Before the evening was out the camp had taught the colony one of its songs.

li.label: Send thanks, but stay home
li.outcome: The colony sends its thanks and stays in. The camp's fire burns late, and the singing carries across the fields.

texts.li: The tree is down, which is half the trouble. {A_nameDef} had marked it for the colony's fence, and {X_nameDef} from the camp {PLACE} felled it for the camp's fire before {A_nameDef} got there with an axe.\n\nThey both came to the council about it, separately, within the hour.

[camp:Hunters] {A_nameDef} tracked a deer all morning and was lining up the shot when {X_nameDef} from the hunters' camp {PLACE} took it first. Now they both claim the carcass, loudly, and the camp and the colony are watching to see what the council says.

[river] {X_nameDef} from the camp {PLACE} has been drawing water from the colony's side of the river, and {A_nameDef} has had enough of it. There were words at the water's edge this morning, and both of them want the council to settle it.
[summer] It's hot, tempers are short, and {A_nameDef} caught {X_nameDef} from the camp {PLACE} picking berries the colony had been waiting on for a week. The argument could be heard from the fields.

[winter] Firewood is precious in winter, and {A_nameDef} found {X_nameDef} from the camp {PLACE} gathering deadwood the colony had stacked to dry. {X_nameDef} says it was lying loose. {A_nameDef} says it was a stack.

[camp:Prospectors] {X_nameDef} from the prospectors' camp {PLACE} dug a test hole right across the path {A_nameDef} uses to the fields, and {A_nameDef} found it in the dark, with one leg. {A_nameDef} isn't hurt, but wants the council to say something.

li.label: Back {A_nameDef}: the camp must make it good
li.outcome: The council took {A_nameDef}'s side, and {X_nameDef} went back to the camp with a face like thunder. They'll make it good, they say. The camp has been cooler toward the colony since.

outcomes.li: [camp:Hunters] The council gave the deer to {A_nameDef}. The hunters took it badly, and the colony's dogs are being growled at.

li.label: Let them have it, this once
li.outcome: The council lets the camp have it, as a gift between neighbors. {X_nameDef} is gracious about it. {A_nameDef} is not.

outcomes.li: [trait:Kind] The council lets the camp have it. {A_nameDef} shrugs and says {A_pronoun} would have offered anyway.

li.label: Have our best talker sort it out between them
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} walked {A_nameDef} and {X_nameDef} down to the spot and had them split the difference: half each, and a handshake the whole camp could see. It held.

outcomes.li: [b:office:Speaker] {B_nameDef}, as the colony's speaker, heard both of them out at the camp's fire and gave a judgment both sides could live with. The camp nodded along.

li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} tried to find a middle way, and found that {A_nameDef} and {X_nameDef} both thought they were already standing on it. It went round in circles until dark.
